_note: Static country-level markers for networks with no physical station pins. Consumed by index.html alongside stations.json. THIS FILE IS USER-FACING: every `note` and `yearly_cost` string renders directly in map popup tooltips for hobbyists. See `_note_field_convention` and `_yearly_cost_convention` below before editing.
_rules_doc: Process and editing rules: country_markers.proc.md (same dir). Pipeline context (how this file relates to docs/networks.md and docs/country-survey.md): ../docs/pipeline.md.
_note_field_convention: The popup auto-renders the access label, yearly_cost, region, note, and registration URL — so `note` should ADD information beyond those, not restate them. DO NOT: repeat the price (it's in yearly_cost), repeat the access label ('Paid subscription required' is already shown), restate the region, include the registration URL inline (it renders separately), or instruct the user to 'contact X' (link to the website via `registration` instead). DO include, when applicable: station count once ('78 stations'), free hobbyist alternatives ('Volunteer rtk2go/Centipede bases provide partial free coverage'), terminal access blockers in plain words, real safety/operational warnings, non-obvious access mechanics. Tone: matter-of-fact, hobbyist-addressed, ≤2 short sentences typical, ~250 chars max. Skip the field entirely if there's nothing useful to add.
_yearly_cost_convention: Single short line, one of: '$X/yr' (USD), '€X/yr (~$Y/yr)' / '£X/yr' / '¥X/yr' / '₹X/yr' / '₽X/yr' / 'S$X/yr' (symbol currencies), or 'X CCY/yr (~$Y/yr)' for ISO-only codes (CHF, SEK, NOK, RSD, etc.). Drop the '~' prefix unless the figure is genuinely uncertain (estimates are implicit). If pricing is not published, OMIT the field entirely so the line disappears from the popup — do not write 'pricing not publicly listed' there. Multi-tier pricing: lead with the primary tier; mention any hobbyist-relevant secondary tier in `note`. Local-currency qualifiers (e.g. 'private users only') belong in `note`, not `yearly_cost`.
_tiers: Five values describing the network's nature from a hobbyist's perspective: 'free' (no fee to use; coloured circle if in-pipeline + has data, grey circle otherwise; note must truthfully open with 'N stations, free.' when no data is ingested yet); 'paid' (commercial subscription, hobbyist can buy access; circled-? marker; yearly_cost recommended); 'paid-affordable' (paid but under ~$200/yr or otherwise hobbyist-reachable; circled-? marker); 'restricted' (no hobbyist path at any price — vetted partners, sector-only, no published rate; circled-? marker); 'weird' (something interesting to a target user that doesn't fit the other tiers — non-standard NTRIP, active jamming/spoofing, infrastructure too sparse to work, war-disrupted, free RINEX-only PPK alternative without real-time NTRIP, network announced/under construction but not yet operational, government CORS distributed only via licensed commercial resellers, micro-state with no local service; circled-? marker, note carries the explanation). The tier drives marker style; whether station data exists is derived at runtime from stations.json (in-pipeline + data → coloured pins/circle; otherwise → grey circle for free, circled-? for the others).
_vrs_flag: Optional 'vrs': true means the network delivers VRS / network-RTK streams (a virtual reference station near the rover) rather than a single physical antenna. Orthogonal to tier — a network can be free+vrs (KSA-CORS, SAPOS), paid+vrs (swipos, HEPOS), restricted+vrs (DVRS, KazGeoDesy), etc. Absence of the flag means nothing — either the network is single-base, or VRS-status is unknown / not relevant. The flag is informational; the renderer uses it together with data presence to decide visuals (free+vrs+ingested → coloured ring; free+vrs+not-ingested → grey ring; non-VRS free entries with pins fall through to physical pins from stations.json).

markers.name: ASG-EUPOS
markers.note: Free since 2 Oct 2022. Account approval takes 1–2 working days.

markers.name: CROPOS
markers.note: Free since April 2022. One-time 40 EUR registration fee.

markers.name: ESTPOS
markers.note: Currently free through 31 Aug 2026; pricing afterwards not announced. A signed service agreement via the portal is required.

markers.name: ReNEP
markers.note: Coverage includes mainland Portugal, the Azores, and Madeira.

markers.name: ZAKPOS
markers.note: Price is a reduced wartime rate (April 2025). Streams pause automatically during air-raid alerts.

markers.name: UA-System.NET
markers.note: Shorter subscription terms available. Wartime discount for eastern and southern oblasts.

markers.name: RTK HUB
markers.note: Caster address issued after registration. Price is a reduced wartime rate.

markers.name: Kyivstar mAgri.RTK
markers.note: Sold only bundled with a Kyivstar mobile contract, not as a standalone subscription. Streams pause during air-raid alerts.

markers.name: GPSBru / AGN
markers.note: Single station at Uccle observatory; caster address issued after registration. Useful within ~20 km of Brussels.

markers.name: UGRF CORS
markers.note: Single-base, VRS, MAC (including iMAX), and FKP mountpoints offered.

markers.name: ETCORS
markers.note: Launched Dec 2024 by the Space Science and Geospatial Institute; expansion to ~200 stations planned. No public caster address or access terms yet — contact SSGI directly.

markers.name: Muya CORS
markers.yearly_cost_comment: normalized cost based on 250h use per year, replace when more pricing options become known
markers.note: Pay-as-you-go vouchers via M-Pesa. Longer hourly, daily, and monthly tiers are offered at checkout but not itemised publicly. Payment needs a Kenyan mobile-money account.

markers.name: BF-CORS
markers.note: Free RINEX for post-processing only; no real-time NTRIP service. Active armed conflict covers an estimated 40–60% of the country.

markers.name: KyrPOS
markers.note: Sign-up is a paper-contract flow: download, post, bank transfer; needs a local postal address and bank account. Minimum 1-month subscription. The caster appears geo-filtered outside Kyrgyzstan.

markers.name: Khmer GEONET
markers.note: Free trial through 1 Jul 2026. Stations are 100–200 km apart, so RTK only works close to each site. Caster address issued via the portal.

markers.name: Myanmar Survey Department CORS
markers.note: Government geodetic network used internally; no public caster or registration. No free RTK base within useful range from neighbouring countries — plan to deploy a local base.

markers.name: PACI / Kuwait Municipality CORS
markers.note: Streams issued only to licensed surveying firms under a municipal contract. No public caster address.

markers.name: Lands & Survey CORS
markers.note: An RTK subscription exists, but neither caster address nor price is published. Access runs through the Chief Surveyor's office — apply directly. The tiered prices on caymanlandinfo.ky are for mapping data and do not include RTK.

markers.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
markers.note: No national RTK service. UWI Seismic Research Centre runs scientific GNSS sites on St. Kitts and Nevis but does not stream corrections. The nearest free real-time base is an EarthScope station on Redonda, ~35 km south of Nevis (non-commercial use only).

markers.name: DOL LandGNSS
markers.note: Currently a free trial. Registration requires a 13-digit Thai national ID card number; foreign visitors without one cannot self-register. A handful of volunteer rtk2go bases inside Thailand are open to anyone.

markers.name: TPOS
markers.note: Self-service registration; no professional licence required. 1-year RINEX archive available for post-processing.

markers.name: STPOS
markers.note: Open to anyone, no professional licence required. ID and an intended-use declaration are needed to activate RTK; RINEX is available immediately.

markers.name: Rete GNSS Veneto
markers.note: Open to any user; credentials emailed after registration. Multiple stream formats available.

markers.name: Rete GNSS Liguria
markers.note: 7 stations in Liguria plus 3 shared with SPIN3 GNSS along the northern border.

markers.name: Sicili@net
markers.note: INGV Catania seismic network; credentials emailed after registration. Single-base and VRS streams available.

markers.name: SARNET
markers.note: Sardinia-specific commercial network (SARNET s.r.l.). RTK, VRS, DGPS, and a RINEX archive.

markers.name: HxGN SmartNet Italy (ItalPOS)
markers.note: Covers gaps in Italy's free regional networks, notably Sardinia and northern Calabria. Sold under the ItalPOS brand.

markers.name: ACORN
markers.note: Four regional VRS solutions (South Central, Interior, Southeast, Northwest), a Norton Sound experimental VRS, and a nearest-station single-base stream. Self-service registration, no licence required.

markers.name: NPS CORS
markers.note: Single-base streams across the continental US, Alaska, Hawaii, American Samoa, and the Marianas. Operated by the National Park Service; credentials are issued manually and access outside NPS partner organisations is not guaranteed.

markers.name: REMOS
markers.note: IGVSB lists ~8 active stations but publishes no caster address. GPS jamming around Venezuelan airspace was reported Sep 2025 – Feb 2026 (FAA advisory, MAIQUETIA FIR), so any RTK solution may be intermittent.

markers.name: RED-GEO CORS NTRIP
markers.note: About 7 stations covering La Paz, Cochabamba, Oruro, Sacaba, Tarija, Santa Cruz, and Yacuiba. Sign-up is by phone; no self-service portal or published pricing.

markers.name: HEPOS
markers.note: Cheaper tiers: €160/quarter (~$170) for seasonal use, or a pay-per-minute bundle (€90+VAT). Individual sign-up online; no professional licence required.

markers.name: URANUS / TopNET Live Greece
markers.note: Covers Greece and Cyprus. 3-day free trial available.

markers.name: ROMPOS
markers.note: Price includes VAT. Monthly subscription also available at 100 RON/mo.

markers.name: Orphéon
markers.note: Commercial VRS network; individual subscriptions available. France also has the volunteer Centipede network (crtk.net:2101), free and nationwide.

markers.name: Teria
markers.note: Operated by Exagone SAS for the Ordre des Géomètres-Experts. France also has the volunteer Centipede network (crtk.net:2101), free and nationwide.

markers.name: swipos
markers.note: At this price a local base station is often more practical. Volunteer bases on the Swiss plateau give partial free coverage; pay-per-use CHF 0.50/min is available.

markers.name: CPOS / ETPOS
markers.note: Agriculture tier 5,000 NOK/yr; surveying tier 11,000 NOK/yr (both ex VAT). 1-month free trial for new customers. Volunteer bases give partial free coverage of populated areas south of ~63°N.

markers.name: SIGNAL
markers.note: An early-payer discount tier is sometimes advertised — confirm with GURS before paying. Volunteer bases give partial free coverage of the country.

markers.name: SWEPOS Network RTK
markers.note: 10-day free trial for new customers. Shorter blocks available (90-day pass, 1,000-minute pot). The bundled DGNSS service is sub-metre only, not cm-grade RTK.

markers.name: SiReNT
markers.note: 3-day trial available; sign-up needs SingPass, which is restricted to Singapore residents.

markers.name: MyRTKnet
markers.note: Cost-recovery service operated by JUPEM under the Survey Act. A single volunteer base near Malacca is the only free alternative inside the country.

markers.name: TUSAGA-Aktif
markers.note: Online registration requires a Turkish TC Kimlik number, so foreign visitors cannot self-register. Monthly (₺1,000) and 6-month (₺6,000) plans available. ₺550 one-time device registration fee. Prices include VAT.

markers.name: VNGEONET
markers.note: Foreigners can register with a passport. Monthly (750,000 VNĐ) and 6-month (4,280,000 VNĐ) plans also available. A free tier applies in areas with >80 km station spacing — anywhere outside the densely covered river deltas.

markers.name: PAGeNet
markers.yearly_cost_comment: normalized cost based on 250h use per year (PHP 100/hr) plus PHP 1,000 one-time registration / 3, replace when an annual tier becomes known
markers.note: Day pass ~$18; 1-month ~$212. PHP 1,000 one-time registration. Outside Metro Manila, payment is by LandBank deposit — a practical barrier for foreign visitors.

markers.name: GNSSnet.hu
markers.note: Occasional use: a 30-day local-radius pass (~€38, within 50 km of one point) or pay-per-minute billing (~€1.20–1.80/hr). One-time €30 registration fee.

markers.name: AGROS
markers.note: Hourly and monthly packages available. Portal is Serbian-language only.

markers.name: GeoNet GEO-RTK
markers.note: Caster at gnss.geonet.bg:2101. Cheapest occasional-use tier is ГеоНет 150 at €15/mo (150 RTK minutes, 24-month contract). Several volunteer single-base stations give partial free coverage of central, northern, and eastern Bulgaria.

markers.name: MONTEPOS
markers.note: Subscription plans from 24 hours to 2 years. Caster address is issued after account creation.

markers.name: SRPOS
markers.note: About 17 stations. Shorter prepaid plans: 10 hours (~$17), 20 hours (~$29), 1 month (~$145). The convertible mark (KM) is pegged 1.95583 to the euro.

markers.name: FBiHPOS
markers.note: Open to private individuals. About 17 stations. 100 KM (~$58) one-time registration fee. Shorter plans: 7 days (~$87), 1 month (~$145). Non-standard caster port 8080.

markers.name: e-GNSS
markers.note: Pay-per-use; annual contracts available for regular users. Caster and portal appear geo-blocked from outside Taiwan.

markers.name: CZEPOS
markers.note: Free for education and government bodies; hobbyists pay the standard tariff. Hourly billing also available: 50 CZK/hr RTK/VRS, 60 CZK/hr DGPS.

markers.name: SKPOS
markers.note: Monthly plans suit short projects. Registration accepts private individuals from most countries — no trade licence required. Free for Slovak public-sector bodies.

markers.name: SoI CORS
markers.note: Free for central/state government and academic users. The paid private subscription requires Aadhaar or PAN, so it is effectively limited to Indian residents.

markers.name: Tamil Nadu State CORS
markers.note: Used internally by the Department of Survey and Settlement for cadastral work. No public NTRIP service. Not part of SoI CORS.

markers.name: Réseau GNSS du Québec (MRNF)
markers.note: 18 free government reference stations, but NOT standard NTRIP — each station is a raw TCP stream (per-station IP:port, CMR+/RTCM 3.2). Standard NTRIP clients will not connect; needs a TCP-capable receiver (e.g. Emlid RS2) or an RTKLIB str2str bridge.

markers.name: BC RTN
markers.note: Subscription portal has been offline pending a BC government website reorganisation; check the registration link for updates.

markers.name: Nova Scotia NSACS
markers.note: Real-time corrections are only sold through commercial resellers (HxGN SmartNet, Can-Net, Brandtnet); there is no direct provincial caster. The listed price is the HxGN SmartNet Atlantic plan; Can-Net and Brandtnet do not publish theirs.

markers.name: SCRTN
markers.note: Coverage extends into bordering Georgia and North Carolina via shared receivers. No professional licence required.

markers.name: NCRTN
markers.note: Credentials are perpetual, not annual. A second login is included; further logins $250 each. Free RINEX download.

markers.name: KeyNetGPS
markers.note: Commercial VRS network covering the whole US Northeast — useful in NH, NJ, PA, DE, MD, DC, and RI, which have no free state caster. Pricing on quote from Keypre or resellers.

markers.name: AlphaRTK
markers.region: US Mid-Atlantic (DE, MD, NJ, PA, DC)
markers.note: No annual plan; cheapest sustained option is the 24-month rolling subscription ($1,595 / 24 mo). 1-week free trial useful for spot jobs.

markers.name: eGPS Solutions RTN
markers.note: Plan C "Flex" ($50/day capped $400/mo) suits occasional use; dual-network Plan A is $2,475/yr. Georgia DOT runs no public caster.

markers.name: TURN GPS
markers.note: Covers Utah and northern Nevada (Reno area) via the Nevada GPS Network. Las Vegas is not covered.

markers.name: MTSRN
markers.note: Free RINEX download; static post-processing does not need a subscription.

markers.name: WSRN
markers.note: Two ports: 2011 for NAD83(2011), 2022 for the new NATRF2022 datum. Government and NGS-cooperator agencies get free access.

markers.name: C4Gnet
markers.note: An unlimited RTK tier is $3,500/yr. A free post-processing RINEX subscription is available separately.

markers.name: CRTN (SOPAC)
markers.note: About 250 stations aggregated by Scripps (UCSD) from SCIGN, BARD, USGS Pasadena, Caltrans CVSRN, OCRTN, and EarthScope. Universities and schools are exempt from the fee. Many stations overlap with the free EarthScope network. Credentials take a week or more to issue.

markers.name: IDOT CORS
markers.note: Announced Nov 2024 with about 70 stations planned; no live NTRIP caster yet. ReIL-NET (Kara Company) is an interim paid option covering Chicagoland and central Illinois.

markers.name: TxDOT CORS
markers.note: TxDOT employees and contractors only.

markers.name: CalRTNS
markers.note: State and county agency partners only.

markers.name: APN
markers.note: Government service (Survey of Israel), open only to licensed surveyors. WARNING: pervasive military GNSS spoofing across Israel and the surrounding region since Oct 2023 — RTK is unreliable regardless of NTRIP access.

markers.name: IGRS
markers.note: Only 7 reference stations spaced 500–800 km apart — far too sparse for RTK. No public NTRIP caster.

markers.name: Pak-Rehber
markers.note: Coverage is Karachi metro only, not nationwide. Operated by SUPARCO Business Solutions for authorised users; no public registration path.

markers.name: SLCORSnet
markers.note: Coverage is mainly the Western Province; island-wide rollout in progress. Bank transfer payment only, which may block non-residents.

markers.name: CORSnet
markers.note: Island-wide commercial network, founded 2014. Self-service registration open to individuals; rates quoted on inquiry. Caster address delivered after payment.

markers.name: SOB VRS
markers.note: VRS solution with stations in Dhaka, Chittagong, Rajshahi, Khulna, Maulavibazar, and Rangpur. Pricing not published; payment via Rocket/bKash/SureCash needs a Bangladeshi mobile-banking account. A volunteer base near Chittagong provides a free single-base alternative there.

markers.name: DrukNet / MiraNet
markers.note: Educational and research accounts are free with a supporting letter from your institution.

markers.name: НЦГПИ / KazGeoDesy
markers.note: Pricing not published — sales-contact only via the rtk.qgeo.kz landing page. Sign-up needs a Kazakh ИИН/БИН ID number and KZT bank transfer; foreign self-registration is not possible. Baselines reach ~180 km outside the Astana–Almaty corridor, beyond useful RTK range.

markers.name: UZPOS
markers.note: State CORS network closed to the public. No free volunteer base within 800 km of Tashkent either — hobbyists need to deploy a local base.

markers.name: ALBCORS
markers.note: Application required; no self-service registration and no published caster address. A commercial alternative, SATNET LIVE (landcoal.com), offers trial access.

markers.name: AzPOS
markers.note: Requires a bilateral service agreement with a government office in Baku; no self-service registration and no published tariff. A single volunteer base provides free coverage of greater Baku.

markers.name: ARMPOS
markers.note: Operated by the Cadastre Committee; access restricted to licensed surveyors. No published caster address and no free RTK alternative in the wider South Caucasus.

markers.name: GEO-CORS
markers.note: Registration open via the operator's online portal; pricing not published — quoted by contact with NAPR.

markers.name: DVRS
markers.note: Operated by Dubai Municipality; application required and limited to surveying professionals. The published caster address may have moved — apply via the GeoDubai portal.

markers.name: SLRB PRN
markers.note: Apply by email using the form on the SLRB page; credentials are issued within 1–2 working days and include the caster address. The service may become paid in future per SLRB's own notice.

markers.name: AL-CORS-Net / SAAP
markers.note: Operated under the Ministry of National Defence; no public registration portal or tariff.

markers.name: REGPMOC
markers.note: Single-base stations under IGN / Ministry of Defence (35+ active). Access requires application and payment to IGN, no online self-service. Individuals are not explicitly excluded, but there is no published path for them.

markers.name: EFT-CORS
markers.note: Day-pass and shorter plans available. 3-day RTK trial. Basic 30-second RINEX is free.

markers.name: RTKNet
markers.note: A different port (6030–6041) is used for each federal district. 3-day trial available.

markers.name: HIVE
markers.note: Aggregator of independently owned stations across Russian regions; station count fluctuates. Pay-per-use: daily RTK per station (prices vary, login required) or hourly post-processing. First ~5 min on each station is free.

markers.name: ГЕОСПАЙДЕР
markers.note: Covers Northwest and Central Russia. Short day/week tiers available. Network RTK is delivered in the local MSK coordinate system.

markers.name: 千寻知寸 Qianxun
markers.note: Multi-constellation, nationwide. Chinese residents can register without a surveying licence. Sign-up needs a Chinese phone number and real-name ID check — no path for foreign visitors without those.

markers.name: 中国移动CORS
markers.note: Operated by China Mobile; sign-up is bundled with a Chinese mobile contract. Chinese residents can register individually. Foreign visitors need a Chinese phone number and real-name ID check.

markers.name: Tencent RTK
markers.note: Enterprise sales only — no self-service pricing. Sign-up needs a Chinese phone number and a Chinese business licence.

markers.name: Re.M.FVG (Marussi)
markers.region: Friuli-Venezia Giulia (Italy) + Slovenian SIGNAL border relays

markers.name: CATNET
markers.note: Run by ICGC, separate from the national ERGNSS network. A single ICGC account is enough; no professional licence required.

markers.name: GRAFCAN REPCAN
markers.note: Pricing not published — see tiendavirtual.grafcan.es. Free Spanish ERGNSS (ergnss-tr.ign.es:2101) also covers the Canaries.

markers.name: InaCORS
markers.note: The caster exposes 4 network-solution mounts rather than individual stations, so the map shows few pins. Coverage is dense on Java and Bali; outer islands (Papua, Kalimantan) have gaps.

markers.name: IGAC MAGNA-ECO
markers.note: Physical single-base streams on port 2102; VRS / network-RTK on port 2101.

markers.name: SPSLux
markers.note: No professional licence required.

markers.name: IceCORS
markers.note: Nearest-station selector and VRS3 network-RTK available.

markers.name: CORS-KOREA
markers.note: Federated single-base feed from 8 Korean agencies. Email-only registration; no Korean ID required. The NTRIP password is the literal string 'gnss', not the portal login password. Accounts are auto-deleted after 50 days of inactivity. The separate NGII network-solution service does require Korean mobile-ID verification.

markers.name: MBC RTK / B-RTK
markers.note: Operated by broadcaster MBC; access is bundled with custom B-RTK receiver hardware sold to fleet and OEM integrators, with no consumer NTRIP signup.

markers.name: APOS
markers.note: Short-term: €20/day for RTK or €2/day for decimetre-grade DGPS. €50 one-time setup fee. Free for Austrian farmers with a registered farm.

markers.name: MIRAI / Go!GNSS
markers.note: 16 stations in Japan; the caster also re-streams ~309 partner stations from Australia, New Zealand, the US, Canada, and others. Free registration plus a separate caster authorisation step. Accounts auto-expire after 365 days of inactivity.

markers.name: sapos RP
markers.note: One-time €100 setup fee on top of the annual charge (already amortised in the figure shown). Farms can use the cheaper R-HEPS tier at €150/device/yr.

markers.name: ACORN
markers.note: Network also includes 1 station in Rhode Island, 2 in southern Massachusetts, and 1 on Long Island, NY — a useful fallback for Rhode Island where no state caster exists.

markers.name: AzCORS
markers.note: 37 ADWR stations plus 15 EarthScope/NPS streams. Free registration via ADWR; caster port confirmed after registration.

markers.name: GCGC RTN
markers.note: Operated by the University of Southern Mississippi Gulf Coast Geospatial Center. No professional licence required for registration.

markers.name: KOPOS
markers.note: One-time €20 registration fee. Monthly (€60) and 6-month (€250) plans also available. Credentials issued inside the portal after account creation.

markers.name: OTC GNSS
markers.note: Coverage is northern Tunisia only; the Saharan south is not served. Shorter terms from 60 TND/day also available.

markers.name: AGRS.NL / AGRS.BES
markers.note: Also covers the BES Islands (Bonaire, Saba, Sint Eustatius). Anonymous access at ntrip.kadaster.nl:2101 (or :443 over TLS). Single-base, not VRS. TU Delft runs a mirror at gnss1.tudelft.nl:2101 with a Netherlands subset.

markers.name: FINPOS
markers.note: Access is granted only for research, with written justification renewable every 3 months. A separate FINPOS DGNSS service is open to anyone but only delivers decimetre accuracy.

markers.name: Rete GPS Emilia-Romagna
markers.note: The previously free regional network has been discontinued; the same physical stations now carry commercial corrections only, via NetGEO and TopNET Live.

markers.name: OS Net
markers.note: Corrections are distributed only through licensed commercial resellers — Leica HxGN SmartNet, Trimble VRS Now, Topcon TopNet Live, AXIO-NET, and others. No direct Ordnance Survey caster.

markers.name: Tailte Éireann GNSS Network
markers.note: Free RINEX for post-processing at gnss.tailte.ie; real-time corrections are sold only through commercial resellers (Trimble VRS Now ~€980–1,390/yr, HxGN SmartNet). Volunteer single-base stations across the country offer free real-time fallback.

markers.name: BIGF Gibraltar
markers.note: Tide-gauge GNSS station; RINEX archive only, no real-time RTK service in Gibraltar.

markers.name: ERGAND / PCAR (Andorra)
markers.note: No Andorran national caster. An EUREF-IP station at Pic de Carroi (~5 km from Andorra la Vella) streams free single-base RTCM via the BKG, ROB, or ASI broadcasters. Spanish ERGNSS (ergnss-ip.ign.es) gives nationwide VRS coverage.

markers.name: San Marino RSMC
markers.note: Single reference station; RINEX is published for post-processing only, with no real-time RTK service.

markers.name: Survey Department Brunei
markers.note: Cadastral CORS used internally; no public NTRIP service.

markers.name: Kadaster Sint Maarten CORS
markers.note: Pricing targets professional surveyors. The nearest free alternative is an EarthScope station on Anguilla (~20 km), for non-commercial use only.

markers.name: RGNA / INEGI
markers.note: INEGI publishes free 15-second RINEX from its stations via anonymous SFTP — post-processing only, no real-time service. Real-time RTK in Mexico is sold by private resellers (Red CORS México, Survey+ MX, TopNET Live México).

markers.name: Red CORS México
markers.note: Coverage spans 60–85+ Mexican cities, resold under several vendor brands. Billed monthly or yearly in MXN; a Mexican phone number and bank account are needed at sign-up.

markers.name: IGN Guatemala Red CORS
markers.note: The national mapping institute publishes free RINEX for post-processing; no real-time NTRIP service.

markers.name: IP CORS Honduras
markers.note: Free RINEX from five government sites (Tegucigalpa, San Pedro Sula, Juticalpa, Siguatepeque, La Ceiba) for post-processing. No real-time NTRIP service.

markers.name: INETER CORS
markers.note: INETER publishes free RINEX for post-processing via the Catastro Físico portal; no domestic NTRIP service. EarthScope hosts two free real-time streams in Nicaragua (Chinandega and central) for non-commercial use.

markers.name: CNR/IGCN CORS
markers.note: Free RINEX for post-processing via the eCNR portal; no real-time NTRIP service.

markers.name: Survey3G NTRIP
markers.note: ~90% national coverage. An EarthScope station near San Salvador is a free real-time alternative for non-commercial use.

markers.name: SIRGAS-CHILE / IGM
markers.note: Free RINEX for post-processing. A real-time NTRIP service was announced in 2025; the public endpoint is not yet live.

markers.name: KollNET
markers.note: Coverage runs from Santiago to Frutillar. A free national service is planned by IGM/SHOA; not yet live.

markers.name: PNG2020 reference stations
markers.note: Scientific reference stations supporting the PNG2020 datum; baselines too long for reliable RTK outside Lae and Port Moresby. A paid NTRIP service has been discussed but is not yet live.

markers.name: Fiji CORS
markers.note: Installed in 2022 across Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, and the outer islands. No public NTRIP caster yet; access policy still being worked out.

markers.name: SENCORS
markers.note: PROCASEF + JICA stations delivering VRS / iMAX corrections; restored March 2026 after a disk failure. Subscription required; tariff not published.

markers.name: CNIGS
markers.note: No public NTRIP service. Successive expansion plans (2015 and 2018) never delivered a live caster. Plan to use PPP corrections or deploy a local base.

markers.name: MI-GLIS CORS
markers.note: Operated by the land registry; paid since July 2024 but tariffs are quote-only and the application workflow targets institutions. No published caster address.

markers.name: Hoda Pro
markers.note: Run by Iran's National Cartographic Center on the IPGN stations. The subscription portal is blocked outside Iran and rates are not published. Sign-up needs an Iranian Melli Code (national ID) and an Iranian bank account.

markers.name: SHAMIM
markers.note: Cadastre-programme network: registration requires an Iranian national ID number, an Iranian mobile number, and a specific GNSS receiver serial. Caster firewalled outside Iran.

markers.name: REPANGOL
markers.note: IGCA CORS network underpinning the national reference frame, installed 2010. No public NTRIP endpoint has ever been published; the repangol.net portal is offline.

markers.name: Madagascar — no national RTK
markers.note: The national mapping agency (FTM) maintains only passive geodetic control — no NTRIP service. Two volunteer bases near Mahajanga and Antananarivo cover ~35 km each; the south coast, far north, and east have no free RTK.

markers.name: Bahamas Lands & Surveys CORS
markers.note: Government CORS deployed ~2020 for the Department of Lands and Surveys; institutional access only, no public NTRIP endpoint.

markers.name: RECI
markers.note: BNETD-CIGN CORS upgraded to RTK in 2022, but the caster address is not public — access through institutional channels only.

markers.name: Ghana National CORS Network
markers.note: Unveiled by the Lands Commission in August 2025. No public NTRIP caster; access is routed through licensed surveyors.

markers.name: IGNTOGO National CORS
markers.note: Made mandatory for all topographic and cadastral work by a March 2026 government communiqué. No published caster address; credentials issued by IGNTOGO on request. The igntogo.tg portal has been unreachable since May 2026.

markers.name: IGN Bénin CORS
markers.note: Caster address is disclosed only after registration via IGN Bénin / CatIS. The service is oriented to cadastral use.

markers.name: ССТП РБ / Belgeodesiya
markers.note: Sign-up requires Belarusian residency and a signed paper contract with Belgeodesiya. Western GNSS hardware import has been blocked under EU/UK/US sanctions since 2022.

markers.name: MOLDPOS
markers.note: No surveying licence required. Free test mountpoints are available with shared credentials moldpos/moldpos — try before subscribing.

markers.name: MAKPOS
markers.note: Galileo-capable since 2020. Subscription rates are not published; a community report of free 3G-mobile access exists but is unconfirmed — contact AREC.

markers.name: Réseau GNSS ANCFCC
markers.note: Licensed cadastral professionals only; no individual sign-up path.

markers.name: itri GNSS Network
markers.note: Morocco's first private GNSS network (launched 2020). Sold to surveying professionals; rates not published.

markers.name: MoSRef
markers.note: Free registration. GPS + GLONASS + BeiDou since 2021. Single-base and VRS; four Hong Kong partner stations extend coverage across the Pearl River Delta.

markers.name: OmanCORSnet
markers.note: Operated by NSGIA. Caster at omancorsnet.gov.om:2101 advertises VRS, MAX, and Nearest mountpoints, but credentials are issued only after manual approval; no confirmed hobbyist path.

markers.name: QCORS
markers.note: Operated by CGIS for licensed surveyors and government users. No public self-registration.

markers.name: GNET
markers.note: Continuous GNSS stations across Greenland for ice-sheet and geodetic research. RINEX is free to download from Dataforsyningen for post-processing; no real-time NTRIP service.

markers.name: Rwanda Geodetic Network
markers.note: Free post-processed RINEX from the RLMUA portal; no real-time NTRIP. Three EarthScope stations near Lake Kivu stream free real-time corrections, useful for western Rwanda.

markers.name: Svalbard — Ny-Ålesund only
markers.note: A volunteer Centipede base at the AWIPEV Arctic research station covers ~20–40 km around Ny-Ålesund. Norway's CPOS does not reach Svalbard, and Longyearbyen has no public RTK — plan for a local base or PPP.

markers.name: Botswana DSM CORS
markers.note: Department of Surveys and Mapping operates ~55 CORS at 30–40 km spacing, covering most of the country. No public caster address; access requires direct DSM engagement.

markers.name: CENACARTA CORS
markers.note: Stations in Maputo, Beira, Chimoio, Tete, Quelimane, Nacala, Lichinga, and Xai-Xai, built for post-processing. No public NTRIP endpoint.

markers.name: ZINGSA CORS
markers.note: Statutory fee of US$200/yr. No published caster address or self-service signup — credentials issued only after direct enquiry to ZINGSA.

markers.name: NIGNET
markers.note: Caster at ntrip.nignet.net:21011, fronted by the MIRAnet portal. Accounts are manually approved and fee-paying; no published tariff. Inter-station baselines of 500–1,000 km exceed useful RTK range until the planned 165-station expansion lands.

markers.name: TTAGN
markers.note: Run by the Surveys and Mapping Division. The gpscors.gov.tt portal no longer resolves externally; access appears to be ministry-internal or limited to licensed surveyors.

markers.name: Umhvørvisstovan GNSS
markers.note: Stations at Klaksvík, Vestmanna, Trongisvágur, and Argir, advertised for surveying and construction firms. No caster address or tariff published — apply by direct contact. Danish GPSnet.dk does not cover the Faroes.

markers.name: ESA CORS
markers.note: Operated by the Egyptian Survey Authority for cadastral and infrastructure work; stations are concentrated in Cairo and the Nile Delta. No public caster or self-service registration.

markers.name: Acnovo NTRIP
markers.note: Private commercial NTRIP provider. Billing cycle (monthly vs per-session) and station count not stated publicly; credentials issued after payment.

markers.name: Yemen GAS
markers.note: Civil conflict since 2015 has halted public geodetic services. The General Survey Authority website is unreachable, and there is no public NTRIP caster, RINEX archive, or volunteer base in Yemen.

markers.name: CYPOS
markers.note: Account profile must be validated in person at a Citizen Service Centre, which is a practical barrier without a Cypriot civil registration number. An EUREF-IP single-base station in Nicosia gives ~30 km of free coverage via the BKG, ROB, or ASI broadcasters.

markers.name: GEOCUBA GNSS
markers.note: Operated by GEOCUBA (MINFAR), running since 2019. An NTRIP service is documented in a 2024 paper but no public caster address or registration portal has been published. US OFAC regulations add a further practical barrier for visitors.

markers.name: GPSnet.dk
markers.note: Denmark's main cadastral VRS network. Weekly, monthly, and annual plans available; price shown only after login. Volunteer single-base stations across Denmark (mostly Jutland) give partial free coverage.

markers.name: RTKconnect
markers.note: FKP and VRS streams; ~10 km average baseline. Approved by Klimadatastyrelsen.

markers.name: NGD / IGN FI CORS (Laos)
markers.note: No public NTRIP service. IGN FI's portfolio page describes a Lao CORS installation but discloses no caster address. Plan for a local base or Galileo HAS.

markers.name: Lesotho (TrigNet ZA fallback)
markers.note: No local caster. The nearest free service is South Africa's TrigNet at trignet.co.za:2101; its closest station in Bloemfontein sits ~210 km from Maseru, too far for cm-grade single-base RTK. Plan for a local base or Galileo HAS.

markers.name: Liechtenstein (swipos / APOS coverage)
markers.note: No Liechtenstein caster. Swiss swipos (paid; CHF 1,500/yr or CHF 0.50/min pay-per-use) covers the country directly. Austrian APOS reaches the eastern half and is free for Austrian farmers via eAMA. Volunteer bases sit 20–60 km away.
